findings.claim: The whole component-fixture bundle now has a hard import of the intelligence addon's link tree (`../../src/addons/intelligence/AskTab`, `askStore`, `messages/en.json`), so every `e2e-components` spec, not only the Ask-thread case, depends on the addon submodule being checked out and on `setup-addons.sh` having run. The developer guide still describes the fixture as importing real components from `src/` with no such prerequisite.
findings.impact: Suppose a developer runs `pnpm test:e2e:components` in a checkout without submodules or without the link tree, or an addon pointer bump breaks a file that AskTab imports. Vite then cannot bundle `fixtures/app.tsx`, and every component spec fails at once, including unrelated layout cases such as page-header, citation seams and the justified grid. This failure is loud rather than silent, and CI now prepares the tree, so it is a workflow and coupling cost, not a wrong result.
findings.evidence: frontend/e2e-components/fixtures/app.tsx:78-80 imports from `../../src/addons/intelligence/`. setup-addons.sh:36-52 is what creates `frontend/src/addons/<name>/`. .github/workflows/ci.yml:306-313 now adds `submodules: recursive` and `./setup-addons.sh` to the frontend-layout job, which is why the job builds at all. docs/developer-guide/testing.md:198-213 ('Components in a browser') lists only `pnpm test:e2e:components` and says nothing about the link tree. build-bundle.ts:28-32 keeps the comment that addon slot modules are not part of the fixture 'because bundling them would assert about whichever addon commits core points at', and the new import now does exactly that for one addon file.
findings.repro: not_reproduced (I could only read the code. In a checkout with no frontend/src/addons/intelligence directory, the relative import in app.tsx has nothing to resolve, so the vite build in buildComponentFixture throws before any spec runs.)

bucket_proposal.reason: No declared invariant (I1–I12) covers how the test harness is wired. It is a coupling and documentation gap that a reader can hit, not a wrong product result.

findings.proposed_fix: Add a line to docs/developer-guide/testing.md under 'Components in a browser' saying that `./setup-addons.sh` (with submodules checked out) must run first.

specification_compliance: The reviewed commit 610ab690b changes only .github/workflows/ci.yml. The frontend-layout job now checks out submodules recursively and runs ./setup-addons.sh before installing dependencies, in the same order as the frontend-static and frontend-shuffled jobs (ci.yml:177-192, 261-276). Without this, the touch point 'frontend/e2e-components/: one case that renders the real AskTab' could not bundle in CI, because the fixture imports the addon through the gitignored link tree.

The removed comment said the job needed no submodules because the fixture sheet's `@source "../addons"` scans a tree that is absent in CI. With the tree present, Tailwind now also scans the addon sources, so the fixture sheet is closer to the production sheet. The REQUIRED needle list in build-fixture-css.ts still guards against a sheet that failed to compile.

The bare imports in AskTab's import graph are react, next-intl, lucide-react and markdown-it (in llmChoice.ts, AskSaveDialog.tsx, AskTab.tsx, AnswerMarkdown.tsx and askNoteFormat.ts). All four have aliases in build-bundle.ts:37-43. Its `@/` imports (FileSaveDialog, lib/api, addonEvents, useWebSocket, Button, MarkdownPreview) resolve through the `@` alias to core src. None goes through the `@/addons/*` stub.
Vite runs without preserveSymlinks, so the fixture's `getAskThread` import and AskTab's own `./askStore` resolve to the same real file, and the polling loop reads the same store the tab writes.

A mental mutation check of ask-thread-desktop.spec.ts against I6: removing `min-h-0` or `overflow-y-auto` from the turns container, or moving the form back above the turns (the old order), breaks the asserts on textarea bottom ≤ panel bottom, box.y ≥ scroller bottom, or scrollHeight > clientHeight. The case therefore guards the layout invariant it claims to guard.
I found no change to the I1–I12 code paths in this commit. The intelligence and knowledge pointers are the same as at r6.
potential_unspecified_behavior: The frontend-layout job does not run `scripts/merge-addon-messages.mjs`. The ask-thread fixture works around this by spreading `intelligenceEn` into its own NextIntlClientProvider, so it does not depend on the merged catalogue. Any later fixture that relies on merged addon messages would get raw keys in this job.

With the link tree present, the e2e-layout fixture sheet now holds rules generated from addon sources (including addon test files that Tailwind scans). The removed CI comment claimed no addon writes a rule the justified grid reads. I did not re-verify that claim against the current addon trees.
regression_risks: A broken intelligence submodule pointer, or a missing file in the link tree, now fails every e2e-components spec in CI, not only the Ask-thread case. The failure is loud, but its blast radius is wider than before.
A version skew between the addon's expected packages and frontend/node_modules (react, next-intl, lucide-react, markdown-it) would go unnoticed, because the aliases force the fixture's copies.

This one is outside this commit, from the branch. In knowledge, the startup trust pass and the note scanner start together. `_mark_declared` filters on (drive, note_path), so if the scanner rewrites a row's note_path between the pass's read and its update, a 204 leaves the row null and the next start declares it again. The extra call is harmless because core never overwrites a reviewed tier, but it departs from I9's 'when, and only when'.
test_coverage: The CI change is itself test infrastructure: it is what lets the I6 layout case (ask-thread-desktop.spec.ts) run in CI at all.

No meta-test checks that the frontend-layout job checks out submodules. If the two new steps were reverted, the components job would fail loudly at bundle time rather than pass silently, so that gap is acceptable.
The AskTabThread.test.tsx, askNoteFormat.test.ts, test_spec_addon_081 and test_spec_addon_084 suites are unchanged since r6. I did not re-assess their coverage in depth this round.
not_verified: I did not run CI, Playwright, vite or setup-addons.sh. That the bundle resolves and the ask-thread case passes in the new job comes from reading the code only.
I did not check that adding addon sources to the Tailwind scan leaves every existing e2e-layout invariant passing (for example, the justified-grid or line-clamp sheet assertions).
I did not check what `enMessages` in fixtures/app.tsx is built from, or whether any other fixture now needs merged addon translations.
I did not re-review the backend and frontend code behind I1–I12 in depth, because this commit does not touch it.
I did not check the knowledge scanner/startup-pass race beyond reading `_mark_declared`.
trajectory: The rounds up to r6 patched the saved-note code detection over and over. r2→r3 replaced the hand-written block classifier with markdown-it tokens, which removed it. r3→r4 added state around the remaining inline scanner. r4→r5 removed that scanner and added sentinel substitution, a new prediction that the substituted text parses like the original. r5→r6 narrowed that prediction by keeping brackets in the sentinel. Since r6, the fix commits add no branch, state or prediction to the file-Ask-thread design. They are develop merges (the YouTube storyboard retry SPEC-ADDON-085, the reading-app design fix), the renumbering and re-approval of the spec to SPEC-ADDON-081..084, INDEX ledger cleanup, docs, and this CI commit. The CI commit removes a stated assumption (that the browser job needs no addons) and adds a dependency on the submodules and link tree. That is new build-time state, but it is not a repeat of anything an earlier round added. The YouTube retry spec went through its own two-step revision: first a removal from the Failed record, then a separate Pending-retry record with atomic consumption. That replaced a race-prone mechanism within one feature's spec review; it was not patched across rounds of this review. Overall, the design is not being patched in this round.
